**Bach's Six Cello Suites**
J.S. Bach's six suites for unaccompanied cello (BWV 1007–1012). Each has six movements, beginning with a prelude and ending with a gigue; the first opens with a famous Prelude of flowing arpeggiated G major chords. The fifth requires the A string to be tuned down to G, and the sixth was written for an instrument with an extra fifth (E) string.

**Yo-Yo Ma**
A Chinese-American cellist born in Paris, a former child prodigy and one of the most famous classical musicians alive, with 19 Grammy Awards. He founded the Silk Road Ensemble, played the solos in the film score for Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, performed John Williams's "Air and Simple Gifts" at Barack Obama's 2009 inauguration, and has recorded the Bach suites several times.

**Pablo Casals**
A Catalan cellist who rediscovered the Bach Cello Suites and made the first complete recording of them (1936–1939). Exiled from Franco's Spain, he often played his arrangement of the Catalan folk song "El Cant dels Ocells" ("The Song of the Birds") as an encore; he also formed a famous piano trio with Alfred Cortot and Jacques Thibaud and wrote the oratorio El Pessebre (The Manger).

**Elgar's Cello Concerto in E minor and Jacqueline du Pré**
Edward Elgar's 1919 concerto, his last major work, became the signature piece of the British cellist Jacqueline du Pré, whose 1965 recording made it famous. Du Pré, who was married to pianist and conductor Daniel Barenboim, had to stop performing at 28 because of multiple sclerosis.

**"The Swan" from The Carnival of the Animals**
The thirteenth and second-to-last movement of Camille Saint-Saëns's Carnival of the Animals, in which the cello plays a slow, graceful melody over rippling accompaniment from two pianos. It is a popular encore piece for cellists.

**Dvořák's Cello Concerto in B minor**
Antonín Dvořák's last concerto (1895), written in New York after he heard Victor Herbert's Second Cello Concerto. It was dedicated to his friend, the cellist Hanuš Wihan, but premiered in London by Leo Stern; its slow second movement begins with soft woodwind chords.

**Mstislav Rostropovich and Shostakovich's cello concertos**
Rostropovich was a great Soviet cellist who premiered both of Dmitri Shostakovich's cello concertos. The First, in E-flat major, opens with the cello playing a four-note motto (G, F-flat, C-flat, B-flat). On the day the Warsaw Pact invaded Czechoslovakia in 1968, Rostropovich played Dvořák's concerto at the Proms in London.

**Saint-Saëns's Cello Concerto No. 1 and Tchaikovsky's Rococo Variations**
Saint-Saëns's Cello Concerto No. 1 in A minor is unusual because its sections are played as one continuous movement. Tchaikovsky's Variations on a Rococo Theme is a set of variations for cello and orchestra in an elegant 18th-century style.

**Haydn and Boccherini's cello concertos**
Joseph Haydn's early Cello Concerto in C major was lost until it was rediscovered in Prague in 1961 by Oldřich Pulkert. Luigi Boccherini, an Italian cello virtuoso, wrote a Cello Concerto in B-flat that is best known in a heavily Romanticized arrangement by Friedrich Grützmacher, as well as the string quintet Night Music of the Streets of Madrid and a famous Minuet.

**Bloch's Schelomo and Bruch's Kol Nidrei**
Two works for cello and orchestra inspired by Jewish music. Ernest Bloch's Schelomo is a "Hebrew rhapsody" in which the cello represents King Solomon, and Max Bruch's Kol Nidrei uses the melody of a prayer chanted on Yom Kippur, with the cello imitating a cantor.

**David Popper**
A 19th-century Bohemian cello virtuoso who wrote the Opus 73 etudes known as the High School of Cello Playing. He also wrote short showpieces for cello such as Spinnlied ("Spinning Song") and Elfentanz ("Dance of the Elves").

**Richard Strauss's Don Quixote**
A tone poem in the form of variations, subtitled "Fantastic Variations on a Theme of Knightly Character," in which a solo cello represents the title knight. A solo viola represents his squire Sancho Panza.

**Villa-Lobos's Bachianas Brasileiras No. 5**
One of nine works by Brazilian composer Heitor Villa-Lobos that blend Bach's style with Brazilian music. The fifth is scored for soprano and an orchestra of eight cellos and includes a famous wordless "Aria."

**The cello in ensembles and orchestral music**
The cello is the lowest instrument in a string quartet and pairs with a harpsichord or organ in Baroque basso continuo groups; its music is written mainly in bass and tenor clef. Five solo cellos open Rossini's William Tell Overture, and the cellos and basses play recitative-like passages in the finale of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

**2Cellos and Sheku Kanneh-Mason**
2Cellos is a Croatian duo of Luka Šulić and Stjepan Hauser famous for YouTube covers of pop songs and film music. Sheku Kanneh-Mason, a young British cellist, performed at the 2018 wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle.
